draft.title: Meditation at Constitution Gardens: A Morning of Loving-Kindness and Mindfulness
draft.body:
On Sunday, September 20, 2026, Bhante Pannakara of the Walk for Peace joined the Buddha Meditation Center of Greater Washington DC for Meditation at Constitution Gardens, a quiet morning of practice on the National Mall. Alongside the Buddhist chaplain at George Washington University and a Bhante from the Buddha Meditation Center, our community gathered to pause together amid the movement and noise of Washington DC.

Guided Loving-Kindness and Grounding Mindfulness Meditation

The morning included a loving-kindness meditation and a grounding mindfulness meditation. Sitting together, participants were invited to settle into the body, notice the breath, and make room for the experience of the present moment with patience and care.

Bhante Pannakara shared a gentle reminder for moments when the mind feels busy: “We’re always trying to push our thoughts away, but our job is to teach the mind to stay still. Welcome your thoughts like guests; they will come and they will leave.”

Rather than treating every thought as something to remove, we can meet it with kindness. Thoughts come, remain for a while, and pass. Each time we return to the breath or the body, we have another opportunity to begin again without judgment.

It was a wonderful day for all of us to sit as a group, share this practice, and experience a little stillness together in the heart of the capital. We are grateful to Bhante Pannakara, the GWU Buddhist chaplain, the Bhante from Buddha Meditation Center, and everyone who joined us.

[[internal link opportunity: upcoming meditation sessions in Washington DC]]

May the peace and goodwill cultivated together continue to support kindness, clarity, and care in the days ahead. We look forward to sitting together again soon.

To learn about upcoming meditation sessions and events at the Buddha Meditation Center of Greater Washington DC, follow our page and visit our website.
